chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever grows hair, let him take good care of it or trim it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on growing and maintaining hair?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the principle of *ihsan* (excellence) in personal appearance, linking grooming to spiritual discipline. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition), where neglecting one's appearance is seen as a form of spiritual or social disarray, while well-kept hair signifies respect for oneself and others.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who takes (grows) hair, so let him make it good and take care of it or trim it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘If one keeps hairs he must maintain them properly or clip them.”’
